title: Schauberger's wartime diary matches the Kammler sites

tellings.quote: I was able to go and visit the Schauberger family and they opened up their files, the family files.

plain: The wartime diary of Viktor Schauberger, an Austrian inventor, is said to place him at the same sites, including Jablonec in what was then Czechoslovakia, used by Hans Kammler, the SS general who ran Nazi Germany's secret weapons projects from 1942 to 1945. The British aviation journalist Nick Cook tells Michels he visited the Schauberger family in Austria and they "opened up their files, the family files" to him. If the match holds, it would tie Schauberger's work to the Nazis' most secret projects, which Cook links to talk of antigravity craft.
